(go-linter-driven-development) META ORCHESTRATOR for any Go code change that should end in a commit (features, bug fixes, refactors).
WHEN: User requests Go code work (implement, fix, add, refactor), mentions "@ldd"/"ldd", or runs a /go-ldd-* command in a Go project.
Runs the five-phase workflow (PREPARE is an autonomous sub-phase, 1.5): DESIGN → PREPARE → IMPLEMENT (per-behavior TDD loop) → FULL LINT (lint-fixer agent) → REVIEW (per slice) → SHIP.

Invoked by @linter-driven-development (Phase 4), by @refactoring (after pattern application), or manually for standalone code review.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/user/ai-coding-rules/go-linter-driven-development/skills/documentation

<objective>
Author and maintain the repo brain: a documentation network where any entry point — a
grep hit on a symbol, a file open, CLAUDE.md at session start — reaches full context
within two hops. Everything normative (the documentation ladder, both network
invariants, the comment policy, the edge policy, the index policy, the OKF
frontmatter/bundle policy, root wiring, doc-root discovery) lives ONCE in
`../../rules/R9-repo-brain.md`; this skill is the
actor that applies it. Templates live in `reference.md` — they are menus, never forms.
</objective>

<philosophy>
**The 5-Year Reader Test**: someone reading this in 5 years doesn't care that "we
fixed a bug where X happened" — they want to know how X works NOW. This holds for
comments as much as docs: a PR number, review item, or "the previous behavior"
narration in a godoc is provenance, not behavior (R9's floor names it a failure
mode).

**Behavior over history**: document what the product DOES, not what changed. A bug fix
updates the affected section to describe correct behavior; it never appends a "Fixed:"
entry (worked examples in reference.md, "Bug Fix Documentation").

**Conciseness over completeness**: a focused doc that gets read beats an exhaustive
doc that gets skipped.

**Plain words over clever words**: everyday English, short sentences, one idea per
sentence. Write for a fresh graduate whose first language may not be English — a
doc that needs a dictionary fails even when it is true (R9's plain-English/empathy
test; applies to godocs and feature docs alike).

**Comments stand alone**: a reader must understand the comment BEFORE reading the
code. If reading the code is required to understand the comment, the comment adds

3	## Principle
4	
5	Documentation is a network ranked by the documentation ladder: storified code →
6	godoc comments → repo docs → the index, each fact placed at the lowest rung that can
7	carry it, higher rungs summarizing and pointing down, never duplicating. Two
8	invariants hold the network together: **reachability** (every doc is reachable from
9	the root: CLAUDE.md → index.md → doc — no orphans) and **bidirectionality** (code
10	points up at its feature doc; docs point down at code via greppable symbols; the
11	index points everywhere). The doc root itself is an Open Knowledge Format (OKF
12	v0.2) bundle: content docs carry YAML frontmatter, a file's path is its identity,
13	and every index line is drift-checked against the `description` one level down
14	(bundle policy below).

16	## Why
17	
18	Each rung of the documentation ladder has its own drift economics. Rung 0 cannot
19	drift — the code *is* the behavior. Rung 1 drifts slowly: a godoc comment lives
20	beside its symbol and gets reviewed with every diff that touches it. Rung 2 drifts
21	on its own unless networked: nothing in a normal diff forces `docs/` open, so a

24	drift-checked (Q7). Placing a fact above its lowest viable rung therefore buys drift for

163	## Design guidance
164	
165	Forward guidance — what @documentation applies when writing docs after a feature.
166	
167	### The documentation ladder
168	
169	| Rung | Layer | Drift | Owns |
170	|---|---|---|---|
171	| 0 | Storified code | none — it IS the behavior | the story; names carry context (owned by `R3-storifying.md`, cited not restated) |
172	| 1 | Code comments (godoc) | low — lives beside the code, reviewed with diffs | the WHY within a tiered 1–5 prose-line budget (policy below); network edges: `See docs/<feature>.md` |
173	| 2 | Repo docs | medium — drifts unless networked | feature/architecture docs in the doc root; point back down via greppable symbol references (edge policy below) |
174	| 3 | The map | minimal — short and drift-checked (Q7) | `index.md` in the doc root: one line per doc, grouped by topic; wired into CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md |
175	
176	(The rung metaphor deliberately mirrors the testing composition ladder in @testing:
177	lowest rung that can carry it, always.)
178	
179	**Placement rule:** document each fact at the lowest rung of the documentation
180	ladder that can carry it; higher rungs summarize and point down, never duplicate.
181	Good overlap: the index says "capped-jitter retries", the feature doc explains the
182	cap math, the godoc states the incident — each level adds detail. Bad overlap: the
183	same paragraph pasted at two rungs; it *will* drift. Before writing any comment,
184	first ask whether a rename or extraction (`R3-storifying.md`) makes it unnecessary —
185	rung 0 beats rung 1.

187	### Comment policy (rung 1 — tiered budget)
188	
189	The WHY is the default content of a doc comment, and it lives inside a hard budget:
190	**1–5 prose lines**, scaled to the symbol's importance. Not all symbols are born
191	equal — the budget forces each comment to carry only the most important facts *for
192	that symbol*; everything else moves up to the feature doc (rung 2), where depth is
193	cheap, and the `See docs/<feature>.md` edge carries the pointer. This is the
194	placement rule made operational at write time.

197	more of these values (the growable catalog with worked examples lives in
198	@documentation's reference.md; this list is the normative set of kinds):

201	- **Wider context** — where this sits architecturally; what depends on it
202	- **Important use cases / flows** — when to reach for it
203	- **Boundary contract** — dos/don'ts, valid inputs, error behavior
204	- **Guarantees** — thread safety, nil handling, invariants
205	- **Network edge** — `See docs/<feature>.md` wiring a critical point into the

210	comment-critic agent enforces them adversarially after writing:

222	     meaning "omitted vs explicit zero", the standard error-wrapping style); the

226	     ("T-04-02", "D-07"), requirement tags ("REQ-SVC-01"), spec section refs
227	     ("spec §4"), "the previous behavior" narration, "matching what
228	     <old system> did". A decoder-ring token fails even when it resolves inside a
229	     repo doc: the reader gets the fact as plain prose and the doc through the
230	     one See-edge — never through a code they must look up.
231	     The floor's lens is the 5-year reader test: a reader five years out cares how
232	     the product behaves NOW, never which PR or review round produced it. History
233	     is rewritten as present-tense rationale ("silently picking one of the TLS

235	     incident/ticket reference survives only when it IS the rationale for a

304	function bodies are R3's (its Q3 — each is an extraction candidate, and the fix is
305	a function named after the comment); doc comments *on* exported symbols are this
306	rule's (Q4 below — they must carry why/context, not restate the identifier).
307	
308	### Edge conventions
309	
310	- **Code → docs** (rung 1 → rung 2): a literal relative path in the comment —
311	  `See docs/retry-policy.md` — always on its own trailing line, never braided
312	  into the summary sentence (the first sentence stays clean: "Package accounts
313	  registers the /accounts REST endpoints.", then the See-line). Paths to docs
314	  are fine; docs move rarely and Q2 verifies them mechanically.
315	- **Docs → code** (rung 2 → rungs 0–1): cite by **exported symbol** (`Policy`,
316	  `ParsePolicy`); a **package or directory path** (`retry/`) only when a location
317	  is genuinely needed; **file paths never, line numbers never** — they are the most
318	  churn-prone coordinates in the repo (`R5-vertical-slice.md`'s slice reshaping
319	  renames and splits files as a matter of course). A renamed exported symbol is a
320	  deliberate, repo-wide-grep act, and a symbol is one grep or IDE-jump from its
321	  file — symbols are the stable coordinates. Cite the **shortest token that greps
322	  uniquely**: bare symbol by default; package-qualify only when the bare name is
323	  ambiguous under repo-wide grep. Headers especially — a header is a landmark, not
324	  a coordinate dump.
325	- **Symbol-less artifacts** (examples/, scripts/, testdata/, configs) are cited by
326	  **directory**, paired with the exported symbols the artifact demonstrates when
327	  any exist — a bare directory link loses drift detection; the paired symbols
328	  restore it.
329	- **Test references** cite the test **package** (`the logger/ package tests`),
330	  optionally its suite entry point (`TestSpanLoggerAPISuite`) — never individual
331	  test functions. Test functions have no external callers and no deprecation
332	  pressure, making them the repo's least stable symbols. Name one only when the
333	  doc's point is that specific test's design.
334	- **Every docs→code edge is a literal, greppable token** — never a prose paraphrase
335	  of code structure. Greppable edges make drift mechanically detectable (Q2);
336	  paraphrases fail silently.
337	- **Edge density stays low**: entry points and key players only. The doc maps the
338	  front doors; it does not mirror the tree. ASCII trees are welcome as orientation
339	  devices at **package/directory granularity** — a directories-only tree is just a
340	  set of package-path citations; file-level leaf entries are the violation. Prune
341	  the leaves, keep the tree.
342	- **Links are one-way — write an edge only when no structure implies it.** A doc's
343	  parent is `index.md` in its own directory, derivable from the path alone: never
344	  write a child→parent backlink, and never a `related:` frontmatter key — body
345	  links ARE the machine-readable graph. Lateral doc→doc links go inline, with the
346	  relationship stated in the sentence that carries the link ("auth retries use the
347	  capped-jitter policy — [retry-policy.md](retry-policy.md)"). The one axis no
348	  structure carries is code↔docs — which is exactly why those edges are written in
349	  both directions and grep-verified (Q2). There is no `## Related` section:
350	  a relationship that cannot find a sentence in the body is not worth an edge.
351	
352	### Frontmatter — the doc root as an OKF bundle (rungs 2–3)
353	
354	The doc root conforms to Open Knowledge Format v0.2 (markdown bundle: one concept
355	per file, path = identity, links form the graph). R9 applies a **stricter profile**
356	on top; every key it requires is a valid OKF key, so the bundle stays consumable by
357	any OKF tool.
358	
359	- **Content docs** carry required `type` (`feature` / `architecture` / `guide` —
360	  the spec's one required key) and `description` (one line — it IS the doc's
361	  index line). Optional: `title` (the H1 is the title; the key never replaces
362	  it), `generated` (OKF's provenance key: ISO 8601, last substantive update),
363	  `tags`, and lifecycle keys `status: draft|stable|deprecated` and `stale_after`
364	  — the frontmatter-native form of the ⚠️ stale flag.
365	- **Indexes carry no frontmatter** — OKF reserves `index.md` and keeps it bare,
366	  with one spec-sanctioned exception: the root index carries `okf_version: "0.2"`
367	  and nothing else. R9 requires that key (profile rule); any other key on any
368	  index is a violation.
369	- **Drift-check rule**: a content doc's index line IS its `description`, copied
370	  verbatim, prefixed ⚠️ when its lifecycle says so (`status: deprecated`, or
371	  `stale_after` in the past) or when a bootstrap pass classified it stale. The
372	  description is the single source; the conformance gate (Q7) fails when an index
373	  line drifts from it. Sub-index lines in the root map are authored (a bare
374	  sub-index has no `description` to copy) — keep them short.
375	- **Never emit `log.md`** — OKF reserves it for change history; this rule is
376	  behavior-not-history, so the file must not exist in a doc root.
377	- **Broken links stay violations** — internally, OKF's dangling-link tolerance
378	  would silence the drift alarm. The *(planned)* marker (Q2) is the one
379	  sanctioned form of a not-yet-written reference.
380	- Copy-pasteable templates (content doc, root index, conventions doc) live in
381	  @documentation's reference.md; only the policy lives here.
382	
383	### The index (rung 3) and the root
384	
385	- `index.md` lives in the doc root and MUST stay short: a concise reference guide,
386	  **one line per doc**, grouped by topic. It is the map, not a doc.
387	- Past ~300 lines it becomes a **map of maps**, and the split is directory-shaped:
388	  each topic becomes a subdirectory with its own bare `index.md` (OKF's
389	  per-directory reserved file), and the root index shrinks to one short authored
390	  line per sub-index. The imported root stays cheap and every doc is still two hops away
391	  (the root map is hop 0 — it rides in with the CLAUDE.md import). The split moves
392	  files, so it lands in the **same commit** as the Q2-driven rewrite of code-side
393	  `See docs/...` paths — a moved doc with a stale code edge is a broken network
394	  between commits.
395	- **Root wiring**: the routing block is authored ONCE, in AGENTS.md — a short
396	  plain block (start at the index; conventions in `<docroot>/conventions.md`) at
397	  the repo root and, in a monorepo, nested per sub-project (closest file wins).
398	  It serves every tool that reads AGENTS.md instead of CLAUDE.md. CLAUDE.md never
399	  duplicates it: it embeds AGENTS.md via `@AGENTS.md` and adds the
400	  `@<docroot>/index.md` import (e.g. `@docs/index.md`) so the map itself is in
401	  context at session start.
402	- **`<docroot>/conventions.md` is the self-hosting doc** (`type: guide`): the
403	  network's own maintenance rules — frontmatter templates, link rules, the
404	  never-list — written for a contributor without this plugin. It is listed FIRST
405	  in the index, one pointer line.
406	
407	### Doc root discovery and monorepos
408	
409	- Discovery order: `.ai/` → `.ainav/` → `docs/`. Use the first that exists; create
410	  `docs/` if none does.
411	- Monorepo: each sub-project (its own `go.mod` or equivalent sub-project boundary)
412	  gets its own doc root and index; the repo-root index links the sub-indexes.
413	  Mechanical discovery is keyed on `go.mod` — a sub-project in another language
414	  keeps its docs reachable through the root index, but is outside the gate's
415	  bundle checks and Q2's code↔docs verification. Everything that touches code
416	  (sub-project discovery, the declaration set, the code-edge grep, the
417	  file-path ban, the symbol shapes) is supplied per language by the gate's
418	  adapter block; this build carries the Go adapter.
419	- Nesting inside a doc root is allowed; the index (or a sub-index) covers every
420	  file in it.
421	
422	## Fix pattern
423	
424	- **Push the fact down a rung**: delete the comment; make a rename or extraction
425	  carry the knowledge instead (`R3-storifying.md`). The cheapest doc is a name.
426	- **Convert WHAT to WHY or delete**: rewrite the doc comment to carry context the
427	  code cannot (rationale, incident, constraint, contract) — or remove it; a comment
428	  that restates the identifier is negative-value.
429	- **Rewire orphan doc**: add its one line to `index.md` *and* add a code-side edge
430	  (`See docs/<feature>.md`) from the package or type it describes — both invariants,
431	  reachability and bidirectionality, in one move.
432	- **Wire the root**: add or repair the AGENTS.md routing block (plain lines
433	  pointing at the index and `conventions.md` — authored once, there) and
434	  CLAUDE.md's two imports: `@AGENTS.md` and `@<docroot>/index.md`. CLAUDE.md
435	  never restates the routing prose.
436	- **Add missing frontmatter**: verify-or-add the required keys on any content doc
437	  that lacks them; copy the `description` into the doc's index line. Strip any
438	  frontmatter an index carries beyond the root's `okf_version`. A `type` that
439	  cannot be inferred from the doc's content is reported for a human call, never
440	  guessed silently.
441	- **Update the stale doc with the behavior change**: rewrite the affected section to
442	  describe current behavior — never append a changelog entry (the
443	  behavior-not-history discipline lives in @documentation).
444	
445	## Falsifying questions
446	
447	Answer each with evidence (`file:line`, command output) — never a bare verdict.
448	Determine the doc root first (discovery order above); `<docroot>` below is that
449	directory. Q1–Q3 and Q7 are fully mechanical: the plugin ships them as
450	`scripts/check-repo-brain.sh` (installed into the repo by the bootstrap pass), so
451	one command answers all four.
452	
453	1. **Is any doc an orphan?**
454	   Detection: `find <docroot> -name '*.md' ! -name 'index.md'` versus the link
455	   targets extracted from `index.md` and any sub-indexes, e.g.
456	   `grep -oE '\]\([^)]+\.md\)' <docroot>/index.md`.
457	   Violation: a doc file no index references — unreachable from the root, so
458	   unread, so rotting. Cite the file and the index that should list it.
459	
460	2. **Is any edge broken — in either direction?**
461	   Detection, code→docs: `grep -rnoE '(docs|\.ai|\.ainav)/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+\.md' --include='*.go' .`
462	   plus `.md`-to-`.md` links inside `<docroot>`; `test -f` each target.
463	   Detection, docs→code: build the repo's declaration set once — single-line
464	   and grouped `type (` / `var (` / `const (` declarations, functions, and
465	   methods — and resolve each backticked symbol against it. A token missing
466	   from the set still resolves when it appears as a whole word in any
467	   non-markdown repo file (config keys, alert names, test helpers). A
468	   package-qualified `pkg.Sym` whose package is not declared in this repo is
469	   external (stdlib, dependencies) and exempt. For a cited package or
470	   directory path, `test -d` it.
471	   Violation: any unresolved target in either direction. Additionally, a doc citing
472	   a **file path or line number** is itself a violation of the edge policy —
473	   regardless of whether the coordinate currently resolves. Exempt from the
474	   ban: URL spans (e.g. pkg.go.dev links), fenced code blocks, and glob
475	   patterns (a span containing `*` is a pattern, not a citation).
476	   Two exemptions, both scoped to symbol resolution and both per-LINE — a line
477	   carrying either marker is skipped whole (the file-path ban has no exemption
478	   beyond URLs): a line carrying the ⚠️ stale flag (cites an unresolved
479	   `Symbol`) is a recorded finding, not a broken edge — the decision to
480	   refresh, remove, or keep it is the user's. And backticks are a resolvability
481	   contract — a future/roadmap symbol is written in prose or explicitly marked
482	   *(planned)*, and a *(planned)*-marked line is exempt from resolution.
483	
484	3. **Is the root unwired?**
485	   Detection: for each doc root, `grep -l '<docroot>/index.md' CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md
486	   2>/dev/null` in the root's owning project directory — the exact path, never a
487	   bare `index.md` mention. A monorepo sub-root also counts as wired when the
488	   repo-root index links into it.
489	   Violation: no hit anywhere — the map exists but is not in context at session
490	   start; the `@<docroot>/index.md` import is missing.
491	   Advisory: CLAUDE.md is wired but AGENTS.md lacks the routing reference — every
492	   tool that reads AGENTS.md instead of CLAUDE.md starts blind.
493	
494	4. **Does a doc comment on an exported symbol state WHAT instead of WHY?**
495	   Detection: for each exported declaration in the diff
496	   (`grep -nE '^(type|func) [A-Z]' <changed files>`), read its doc comment and
497	   compare its tokens against the identifier and the first lines of the body — a
498	   comment whose content is recoverable from the name or the code adds nothing.
499	   Violation: the comment restates the identifier (`// Policy is a policy`) or
500	   narrates the implementation, instead of carrying rationale, constraints, or
501	   context the code cannot. Boundary: block comments *inside* function bodies are
502	   NOT this question — they are `R3-storifying.md` Q3 (extraction candidates).
503	
504	5. **Is new exported API naked, or a feature-sized change undocumented at rung 2?**
505	   Detection: in the diff, `grep -nE '^(type|func) [A-Z]'` on added lines and check
506	   each for a preceding `//` doc comment; separately, compare new packages or entry
507	   points in the diff against `<docroot>` contents.
508	   Violation: a new exported type or package with no doc comment; or a
509	   feature-sized diff (new package, new entry point) with no doc-root entry —
510	   the knowledge shipped without joining the network.
511	
512	6. **Did behavior change silently under an existing doc?** *(advisory)*
513	   Detection: map the diff's changed packages to docs that cite their symbols or
514	   package paths (grep `<docroot>` for the package name and its exported symbols);
515	   check whether any such doc is in the diff.
516	   Violation (advisory): a package with a citing feature doc changed and the doc
517	   did not — flag it with the doc's path as evidence; the fix is updating the
518	   affected section, never appending history.
519	
520	7. **Does any file break the bundle contract?**
521	   Detection: every content `.md` under `<docroot>` starts with a terminated
522	   frontmatter block (first line `---`, a closing `---` follows) carrying
523	   `type` valued `feature` / `architecture` / `guide` and a non-empty
524	   `description`. Index files carry NO frontmatter — except the root index,
525	   whose block is exactly one `okf_version: "0.2"` (required there, forbidden
526	   everywhere else). `grep -rn '^related:'` over doc-root
527	   frontmatter; `find <docroot> -name 'log.md'`. For every index line shaped
528	   `- [doc](path) — text`, compare the text against the target's `description`
529	   when it has one (⚠️-flagged lines exempt — recorded findings, not copies;
530	   bare sub-index targets have no `description` and are skipped); the script's
531	   `--fix` flag rewrites drifted lines from the descriptions.
532	   Violation: a missing or unterminated frontmatter block on a content doc; a
533	   missing or invalid required key (a `type` outside the three classes, an
534	   empty `description`); frontmatter on a sub-index; any key besides
535	   `okf_version` on the root index; a missing, duplicated, or mis-valued root
536	   `okf_version`; a `related:` key anywhere; a `log.md` anywhere in the doc
537	   root; an index line that drifted from the `description` it copies.
538	   Advisory branch: a doc whose `stale_after` is in the past (or
539	   `status: deprecated`) with no ⚠️ on its index line — recorded staleness the
540	   map does not show; the fix is re-copying the line (drift-check rule above).

# R9 — Repo Brain (Documentation Network)

## Principle

Documentation is a network ranked by the documentation ladder: storified code →
godoc comments → repo docs → the index, each fact placed at the lowest rung that can
carry it, higher rungs summarizing and pointing down, never duplicating. Two
invariants hold the network together: **reachability** (every doc is reachable from
the root: CLAUDE.md → index.md → doc — no orphans) and **bidirectionality** (code
points up at its feature doc; docs point down at code via greppable symbols; the
index points everywhere). The doc root itself is an Open Knowledge Format (OKF
v0.2) bundle: content docs carry YAML frontmatter, a file's path is its identity,
and every index line is drift-checked against the `description` one level down
(bundle policy below).

## Why

Each rung of the documentation ladder has its own drift economics. Rung 0 cannot
drift — the code *is* the behavior. Rung 1 drifts slowly: a godoc comment lives
beside its symbol and gets reviewed with every diff that touches it. Rung 2 drifts
on its own unless networked: nothing in a normal diff forces `docs/` open, so a
feature doc rots silently — *unless* an edge from the changed code names it and an
index line makes it findable. Rung 3 barely drifts because it is short and
drift-checked (Q7). Placing a fact above its lowest viable rung therefore buys drift for
nothing; placing it below (cramming architecture into a comment) buries it where no
overview reader looks.

The network exists for cold starts. A fresh Claude session — or a new engineer —
enters the repo through one of three doors: a grep hit on a symbol, a file open, or
CLAUDE.md at session start. From any door, full context must be two hops away:
symbol → its godoc → the feature doc; CLAUDE.md → index.md → the feature doc. An
unlinked doc is an unread doc, and unread docs rot — orphaning is not a tidiness
problem, it is the mechanism by which documentation dies. Drift-detection depends on
the same wiring: only a **literal, greppable** edge can be mechanically verified
(Q2 below); a prose paraphrase of code structure can be wrong forever without
anyone noticing.

## Canonical example

A retry feature shipped months ago. The knowledge exists — and is unreachable.

### Before — the knowledge is there, the network is not

```
repo/
├── CLAUDE.md              # build commands only; no reference to docs/
├── docs/
│   └── retry-policy.md    # explains the jitter decision; nothing links to it
└── retry/
    └── policy.go
```

```go
package retry

type Policy struct { // exported, no doc comment
    maxAttempts int
    baseDelay   time.Duration
}

func (p Policy) Do(ctx context.Context, op Op) error {
    // loop over attempts and back off between failures
    for attempt := 1; attempt <= p.maxAttempts; attempt++ {
        if err := op(ctx); err == nil {
            return nil
        }
        delay := p.baseDelay * time.Duration(1<<attempt)
        sleepWithJitter(ctx, delay)
    }
    return ErrExhausted
}
```

```markdown
<!-- docs/retry-policy.md -->
The retry loop lives in retry/policy.go around line 40; it uses full jitter.
```

Four breaks, one per rung: the in-body comment narrates WHAT the next lines do
(a rung-0 failure — the block wants to be an extracted, named function, which is
`R3-storifying.md`'s territory); `Policy` is a naked exported type, so a grep hit
on it dead-ends with zero context (rung 1); `docs/retry-policy.md` is an orphan —
no index lists it, no comment cites it, and it cites code by **file path and line
number**, coordinates that the next refactor invalidates (rung 2); and CLAUDE.md
imports nothing, so a fresh session starts blind (rung 3).

### After — the same knowledge, networked

```
repo/
├── CLAUDE.md              # @docs/index.md
├── docs/
│   ├── index.md           # one line per doc, grouped by topic
│   └── retry-policy.md    # points down at symbols, not files
└── retry/
    └── policy.go
```

```go
// Policy is a capped exponential-backoff retry policy with full jitter.
// Jitter is deliberate: synchronized clients retrying in lockstep re-overloaded
// the upstream API after every blip. See docs/retry-policy.md for the incident
// and the cap math.
type Policy struct {
    maxAttempts int
    baseDelay   time.Duration
}

func ParsePolicy(maxAttempts int, baseDelay time.Duration) (Policy, error) {
    if maxAttempts < 1 || baseDelay <= 0 {
        return Policy{}, ErrInvalidPolicy
    }
    return Policy{maxAttempts: maxAttempts, baseDelay: baseDelay}, nil
}

func (p Policy) Do(ctx context.Context, op Op) error {
    for attempt := range p.attempts() {
        if err := op(ctx); err == nil {
            return nil
        }
        p.backOff(ctx, attempt)
    }
    return ErrExhausted
}
```

```markdown
<!-- docs/retry-policy.md -->
---
type: feature
description: why retries use capped full jitter; `Policy` API
---
Entry point: `Policy.Do`. Construction: `ParsePolicy` — validates the cap
against the base delay, so an unbounded backoff cannot exist.
```

```markdown
<!-- docs/index.md -->
---
okf_version: "0.2"
---
# Repo map

**Resilience**
- [retry-policy.md](retry-policy.md) — why retries use capped full jitter; `Policy` API
```

```markdown
<!-- CLAUDE.md -->
@docs/index.md
```

Every break healed at its rung: storifying killed the WHAT-comment — the extracted
names `attempts`/`backOff` carry it (`R3-storifying.md`); `Policy`'s godoc states
the WHY the code cannot (the incident) and carries the upward edge to the feature
doc; the doc points down with the greppable tokens `Policy.Do` and `ParsePolicy` —
no path, no line number — and is listed in the index; CLAUDE.md imports the index,
so the whole map is in context at session start. Grep `Policy` or open CLAUDE.md:
either way, the jitter incident is two hops away. And the index line has one
source of truth: it IS `retry-policy.md`'s `description`, copied verbatim — the
conformance gate (Q7) fails the moment the copy drifts.

## Design guidance

Forward guidance — what @documentation applies when writing docs after a feature.

### The documentation ladder

| Rung | Layer | Drift | Owns |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Storified code | none — it IS the behavior | the story; names carry context (owned by `R3-storifying.md`, cited not restated) |
| 1 | Code comments (godoc) | low — lives beside the code, reviewed with diffs | the WHY within a tiered 1–5 prose-line budget (policy below); network edges: `See docs/<feature>.md` |
| 2 | Repo docs | medium — drifts unless networked | feature/architecture docs in the doc root; point back down via greppable symbol references (edge policy below) |
| 3 | The map | minimal — short and drift-checked (Q7) | `index.md` in the doc root: one line per doc, grouped by topic; wired into CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md |

(The rung metaphor deliberately mirrors the testing composition ladder in @testing:
lowest rung that can carry it, always.)

**Placement rule:** document each fact at the lowest rung of the documentation
ladder that can carry it; higher rungs summarize and point down, never duplicate.
Good overlap: the index says "capped-jitter retries", the feature doc explains the
cap math, the godoc states the incident — each level adds detail. Bad overlap: the
same paragraph pasted at two rungs; it *will* drift. Before writing any comment,
first ask whether a rename or extraction (`R3-storifying.md`) makes it unnecessary —
rung 0 beats rung 1.

### Comment policy (rung 1 — tiered budget)

The WHY is the default content of a doc comment, and it lives inside a hard budget:
**1–5 prose lines**, scaled to the symbol's importance. Not all symbols are born
equal — the budget forces each comment to carry only the most important facts *for
that symbol*; everything else moves up to the feature doc (rung 2), where depth is
cheap, and the `See docs/<feature>.md` edge carries the pointer. This is the
placement rule made operational at write time.

**The Comment Value Toolbox** — a comment earns its lines by delivering one or
more of these values (the growable catalog with worked examples lives in
@documentation's reference.md; this list is the normative set of kinds):

- **WHY, not WHAT** — rationale, incident, constraint the code cannot carry
- **Wider context** — where this sits architecturally; what depends on it
- **Important use cases / flows** — when to reach for it
- **Boundary contract** — dos/don'ts, valid inputs, error behavior
- **Guarantees** — thread safety, nil handling, invariants
- **Network edge** — `See docs/<feature>.md` wiring a critical point into the
  repo brain

**The three-test standard** — every comment (and every rung-2 doc, for test 3)
must pass all three; @documentation applies them at write time and its
comment-critic agent enforces them adversarially after writing:

1. **Toolbox-value test**, two-sided:
   - *Floor (delete test):* a prose line that delivers none of the toolbox values
     is trash — cut it. Named failure modes: restated identifiers, generic filler
     ("provides validation functionality"), narrated implementation, menu sections
     filled without earning their place, **review-defense narration** — the
     writer arguing with an imagined reviewer ("bounds-checked: it never indexes
     an empty slice", "deliberately narrow — not a generalized table"); a design
     choice that needs defending is defended in the feature doc, not at the code
     line — **restated repo idiom** — a comment
     justifying a convention the repo already applies everywhere (a pointer field
     meaning "omitted vs explicit zero", the standard error-wrapping style); the
     convention is documented once at rung 2 (coding standards), never
     re-explained at each use site — and **provenance and decoder-ring
     references** — PR numbers, review items, plan/decision/test-plan IDs
     ("T-04-02", "D-07"), requirement tags ("REQ-SVC-01"), spec section refs
     ("spec §4"), "the previous behavior" narration, "matching what
     <old system> did". A decoder-ring token fails even when it resolves inside a
     repo doc: the reader gets the fact as plain prose and the doc through the
     one See-edge — never through a code they must look up.
     The floor's lens is the 5-year reader test: a reader five years out cares how
     the product behaves NOW, never which PR or review round produced it. History
     is rewritten as present-tense rationale ("silently picking one of the TLS
     options could apply a mode the caller did not ask for"), and an
     incident/ticket reference survives only when it IS the rationale for a
     constraint — never as provenance.
   - *Ceiling (smart choice):* the comment as a whole must carry the
     highest-value toolbox items for that symbol's tier within its budget. A
     crossroads whose five lines are all boundary trivia while the architectural
     WHY is missing fails, even though each line individually "adds something".
2. **Budget test** — the comment fits its tier budget (accounting and tiers
   below).
3. **Plain-English test (the empathy test)** — write for a fresh graduate whose
   first language may not be English: everyday words, short sentences, one idea
   per sentence. A comment that needs a dictionary fails even when true and
   within budget. Failure modes: fancy vocabulary where a common word exists
   ("utilize" → "use", "leverages" → "uses"), stacked clauses, academic phrasing,
   and unexplained acronyms or insider jargon ("DTO", "tristate") — in the
   comment AND in the symbol name it documents.
   The test has a second half, **self-standing**: the comment must be
   understandable BEFORE reading the code. If the reader must read the code — or
   another comment ("see X's doc comment for why") — to understand this comment,
   it has negative value. State the fact in place; forward references to other
   comments fail.

**Budget accounting** — prose lines count; these are free:

- blank `//` separator lines
- the `See docs/<feature>.md` network-edge line — free ONLY as its own trailing
  line; a doc reference woven into a prose sentence is not an edge, it is clutter
  in that sentence's line count
- short inline example lines, bounded at 2–4 lines — anything bigger belongs in an
  `Example_*` testable example

**Role-based tiers** — judge the tier from the symbol's role in the code:

| Tier | Role signals | Budget | Typical content |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Helper** | small method, plain constructor, obvious accessor | 0–1 prose line | one-line summary; tiny example only if it clarifies |
| **Contract** | parsing constructor (`ParsePolicy`, `ParsePort`), self-validating type, ordinary exported API | 2–3 prose lines | WHY + boundary contract; dos/don'ts example (free) |
| **Crossroads** | entry point, orchestrator, state machine, feature front door | up to 5 prose lines | WHY, architectural context, use cases + See-edge |

**Visibility default — unexported symbols get no comment.** The tier table
prices exported API. An unexported function, type, constant, or variable
defaults to **zero** comment lines: the name is the documentation, and a name
that needs a comment wants a rename or an extraction first
(`R3-storifying.md`). The special case is **one line carrying a very
high-value toolbox item** — a constraint or fact the code cannot carry: an
ordering requirement, an external library quirk, the WHY of a magic number,
the package's one real policy. If a private symbol seems to need more than
that one line, the knowledge belongs to the exported symbol that uses it, the
package doc, or the feature doc. Case file:
`../examples/private-comment-noise.md` — nine commented private helpers;
four survive as one-liners, five get nothing.

**Two bounded escape hatches:**

- **Package docs in `doc.go`**: a package that genuinely earns more (data-flow
  sketch, core-types list, design decisions all pulling their weight) moves its
  package godoc to a dedicated `doc.go`, bounded at ~20–30 lines. A package comment
  inline in a regular file stays within the standard budget.
- **Crossroads expand recommendation**: the writer never self-exceeds the 5-line
  cap. When a critical crossroads would benefit from richer inline godoc beyond the
  doc reference, write within budget and append an optional, end-of-report
  recommendation — `consider expanding <Symbol>'s godoc inline — <rationale>` —
  for a human to decide later (@documentation's report carries it).

Never fill a template for its own sake — @documentation's templates are menus to
pick from, not forms to fill, and the tier budget caps how much of a menu any one
symbol can order. The one near-constant is the network edge: keep the
`See docs/<feature>.md` reference whenever a feature doc exists.

Boundary with `R3-storifying.md`, stated precisely: block comments *inside*
function bodies are R3's (its Q3 — each is an extraction candidate, and the fix is
a function named after the comment); doc comments *on* exported symbols are this
rule's (Q4 below — they must carry why/context, not restate the identifier).

### Edge conventions

- **Code → docs** (rung 1 → rung 2): a literal relative path in the comment —
  `See docs/retry-policy.md` — always on its own trailing line, never braided
  into the summary sentence (the first sentence stays clean: "Package accounts
  registers the /accounts REST endpoints.", then the See-line). Paths to docs
  are fine; docs move rarely and Q2 verifies them mechanically.
- **Docs → code** (rung 2 → rungs 0–1): cite by **exported symbol** (`Policy`,
  `ParsePolicy`); a **package or directory path** (`retry/`) only when a location
  is genuinely needed; **file paths never, line numbers never** — they are the most
  churn-prone coordinates in the repo (`R5-vertical-slice.md`'s slice reshaping
  renames and splits files as a matter of course). A renamed exported symbol is a
  deliberate, repo-wide-grep act, and a symbol is one grep or IDE-jump from its
  file — symbols are the stable coordinates. Cite the **shortest token that greps
  uniquely**: bare symbol by default; package-qualify only when the bare name is
  ambiguous under repo-wide grep. Headers especially — a header is a landmark, not
  a coordinate dump.
- **Symbol-less artifacts** (examples/, scripts/, testdata/, configs) are cited by
  **directory**, paired with the exported symbols the artifact demonstrates when
  any exist — a bare directory link loses drift detection; the paired symbols
  restore it.
- **Test references** cite the test **package** (`the logger/ package tests`),
  optionally its suite entry point (`TestSpanLoggerAPISuite`) — never individual
  test functions. Test functions have no external callers and no deprecation
  pressure, making them the repo's least stable symbols. Name one only when the
  doc's point is that specific test's design.
- **Every docs→code edge is a literal, greppable token** — never a prose paraphrase
  of code structure. Greppable edges make drift mechanically detectable (Q2);
  paraphrases fail silently.
- **Edge density stays low**: entry points and key players only. The doc maps the
  front doors; it does not mirror the tree. ASCII trees are welcome as orientation
  devices at **package/directory granularity** — a directories-only tree is just a
  set of package-path citations; file-level leaf entries are the violation. Prune
  the leaves, keep the tree.
- **Links are one-way — write an edge only when no structure implies it.** A doc's
  parent is `index.md` in its own directory, derivable from the path alone: never
  write a child→parent backlink, and never a `related:` frontmatter key — body
  links ARE the machine-readable graph. Lateral doc→doc links go inline, with the
  relationship stated in the sentence that carries the link ("auth retries use the
  capped-jitter policy — [retry-policy.md](retry-policy.md)"). The one axis no
  structure carries is code↔docs — which is exactly why those edges are written in
  both directions and grep-verified (Q2). There is no `## Related` section:
  a relationship that cannot find a sentence in the body is not worth an edge.

### Frontmatter — the doc root as an OKF bundle (rungs 2–3)

The doc root conforms to Open Knowledge Format v0.2 (markdown bundle: one concept
per file, path = identity, links form the graph). R9 applies a **stricter profile**
on top; every key it requires is a valid OKF key, so the bundle stays consumable by
any OKF tool.

- **Content docs** carry required `type` (`feature` / `architecture` / `guide` —
  the spec's one required key) and `description` (one line — it IS the doc's
  index line). Optional: `title` (the H1 is the title; the key never replaces
  it), `generated` (OKF's provenance key: ISO 8601, last substantive update),
  `tags`, and lifecycle keys `status: draft|stable|deprecated` and `stale_after`
  — the frontmatter-native form of the ⚠️ stale flag.
- **Indexes carry no frontmatter** — OKF reserves `index.md` and keeps it bare,
  with one spec-sanctioned exception: the root index carries `okf_version: "0.2"`
  and nothing else. R9 requires that key (profile rule); any other key on any
  index is a violation.
- **Drift-check rule**: a content doc's index line IS its `description`, copied
  verbatim, prefixed ⚠️ when its lifecycle says so (`status: deprecated`, or
  `stale_after` in the past) or when a bootstrap pass classified it stale. The
  description is the single source; the conformance gate (Q7) fails when an index
  line drifts from it. Sub-index lines in the root map are authored (a bare
  sub-index has no `description` to copy) — keep them short.
- **Never emit `log.md`** — OKF reserves it for change history; this rule is
  behavior-not-history, so the file must not exist in a doc root.
- **Broken links stay violations** — internally, OKF's dangling-link tolerance
  would silence the drift alarm. The *(planned)* marker (Q2) is the one
  sanctioned form of a not-yet-written reference.
- Copy-pasteable templates (content doc, root index, conventions doc) live in
  @documentation's reference.md; only the policy lives here.

### The index (rung 3) and the root

- `index.md` lives in the doc root and MUST stay short: a concise reference guide,
  **one line per doc**, grouped by topic. It is the map, not a doc.
- Past ~300 lines it becomes a **map of maps**, and the split is directory-shaped:
  each topic becomes a subdirectory with its own bare `index.md` (OKF's
  per-directory reserved file), and the root index shrinks to one short authored
  line per sub-index. The imported root stays cheap and every doc is still two hops away
  (the root map is hop 0 — it rides in with the CLAUDE.md import). The split moves
  files, so it lands in the **same commit** as the Q2-driven rewrite of code-side
  `See docs/...` paths — a moved doc with a stale code edge is a broken network
  between commits.
- **Root wiring**: the routing block is authored ONCE, in AGENTS.md — a short
  plain block (start at the index; conventions in `<docroot>/conventions.md`) at
  the repo root and, in a monorepo, nested per sub-project (closest file wins).
  It serves every tool that reads AGENTS.md instead of CLAUDE.md. CLAUDE.md never
  duplicates it: it embeds AGENTS.md via `@AGENTS.md` and adds the
  `@<docroot>/index.md` import (e.g. `@docs/index.md`) so the map itself is in
  context at session start.
- **`<docroot>/conventions.md` is the self-hosting doc** (`type: guide`): the
  network's own maintenance rules — frontmatter templates, link rules, the
  never-list — written for a contributor without this plugin. It is listed FIRST
  in the index, one pointer line.

### Doc root discovery and monorepos

- Discovery order: `.ai/` → `.ainav/` → `docs/`. Use the first that exists; create
  `docs/` if none does.
- Monorepo: each sub-project (its own `go.mod` or equivalent sub-project boundary)
  gets its own doc root and index; the repo-root index links the sub-indexes.
  Mechanical discovery is keyed on `go.mod` — a sub-project in another language
  keeps its docs reachable through the root index, but is outside the gate's
  bundle checks and Q2's code↔docs verification. Everything that touches code
  (sub-project discovery, the declaration set, the code-edge grep, the
  file-path ban, the symbol shapes) is supplied per language by the gate's
  adapter block; this build carries the Go adapter.
- Nesting inside a doc root is allowed; the index (or a sub-index) covers every
  file in it.

## Fix pattern

- **Push the fact down a rung**: delete the comment; make a rename or extraction
  carry the knowledge instead (`R3-storifying.md`). The cheapest doc is a name.
- **Convert WHAT to WHY or delete**: rewrite the doc comment to carry context the
  code cannot (rationale, incident, constraint, contract) — or remove it; a comment
  that restates the identifier is negative-value.
- **Rewire orphan doc**: add its one line to `index.md` *and* add a code-side edge
  (`See docs/<feature>.md`) from the package or type it describes — both invariants,
  reachability and bidirectionality, in one move.
- **Wire the root**: add or repair the AGENTS.md routing block (plain lines
  pointing at the index and `conventions.md` — authored once, there) and
  CLAUDE.md's two imports: `@AGENTS.md` and `@<docroot>/index.md`. CLAUDE.md
  never restates the routing prose.
- **Add missing frontmatter**: verify-or-add the required keys on any content doc
  that lacks them; copy the `description` into the doc's index line. Strip any
  frontmatter an index carries beyond the root's `okf_version`. A `type` that
  cannot be inferred from the doc's content is reported for a human call, never
  guessed silently.
- **Update the stale doc with the behavior change**: rewrite the affected section to
  describe current behavior — never append a changelog entry (the
  behavior-not-history discipline lives in @documentation).

## Falsifying questions

Answer each with evidence (`file:line`, command output) — never a bare verdict.
Determine the doc root first (discovery order above); `<docroot>` below is that
directory. Q1–Q3 and Q7 are fully mechanical: the plugin ships them as
`scripts/check-repo-brain.sh` (installed into the repo by the bootstrap pass), so
one command answers all four.

1. **Is any doc an orphan?**
   Detection: `find <docroot> -name '*.md' ! -name 'index.md'` versus the link
   targets extracted from `index.md` and any sub-indexes, e.g.
   `grep -oE '\]\([^)]+\.md\)' <docroot>/index.md`.
   Violation: a doc file no index references — unreachable from the root, so
   unread, so rotting. Cite the file and the index that should list it.

2. **Is any edge broken — in either direction?**
   Detection, code→docs: `grep -rnoE '(docs|\.ai|\.ainav)/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+\.md' --include='*.go' .`
   plus `.md`-to-`.md` links inside `<docroot>`; `test -f` each target.
   Detection, docs→code: build the repo's declaration set once — single-line
   and grouped `type (` / `var (` / `const (` declarations, functions, and
   methods — and resolve each backticked symbol against it. A token missing
   from the set still resolves when it appears as a whole word in any
   non-markdown repo file (config keys, alert names, test helpers). A
   package-qualified `pkg.Sym` whose package is not declared in this repo is
   external (stdlib, dependencies) and exempt. For a cited package or
   directory path, `test -d` it.
   Violation: any unresolved target in either direction. Additionally, a doc citing
   a **file path or line number** is itself a violation of the edge policy —
   regardless of whether the coordinate currently resolves. Exempt from the
   ban: URL spans (e.g. pkg.go.dev links), fenced code blocks, and glob
   patterns (a span containing `*` is a pattern, not a citation).
   Two exemptions, both scoped to symbol resolution and both per-LINE — a line
   carrying either marker is skipped whole (the file-path ban has no exemption
   beyond URLs): a line carrying the ⚠️ stale flag (cites an unresolved
   `Symbol`) is a recorded finding, not a broken edge — the decision to
   refresh, remove, or keep it is the user's. And backticks are a resolvability
   contract — a future/roadmap symbol is written in prose or explicitly marked
   *(planned)*, and a *(planned)*-marked line is exempt from resolution.

3. **Is the root unwired?**
   Detection: for each doc root, `grep -l '<docroot>/index.md' CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md
   2>/dev/null` in the root's owning project directory — the exact path, never a
   bare `index.md` mention. A monorepo sub-root also counts as wired when the
   repo-root index links into it.
   Violation: no hit anywhere — the map exists but is not in context at session
   start; the `@<docroot>/index.md` import is missing.
   Advisory: CLAUDE.md is wired but AGENTS.md lacks the routing reference — every
   tool that reads AGENTS.md instead of CLAUDE.md starts blind.

4. **Does a doc comment on an exported symbol state WHAT instead of WHY?**
   Detection: for each exported declaration in the diff
   (`grep -nE '^(type|func) [A-Z]' <changed files>`), read its doc comment and
   compare its tokens against the identifier and the first lines of the body — a
   comment whose content is recoverable from the name or the code adds nothing.
   Violation: the comment restates the identifier (`// Policy is a policy`) or
   narrates the implementation, instead of carrying rationale, constraints, or
   context the code cannot. Boundary: block comments *inside* function bodies are
   NOT this question — they are `R3-storifying.md` Q3 (extraction candidates).

5. **Is new exported API naked, or a feature-sized change undocumented at rung 2?**
   Detection: in the diff, `grep -nE '^(type|func) [A-Z]'` on added lines and check
   each for a preceding `//` doc comment; separately, compare new packages or entry
   points in the diff against `<docroot>` contents.
   Violation: a new exported type or package with no doc comment; or a
   feature-sized diff (new package, new entry point) with no doc-root entry —
   the knowledge shipped without joining the network.

6. **Did behavior change silently under an existing doc?** *(advisory)*
   Detection: map the diff's changed packages to docs that cite their symbols or
   package paths (grep `<docroot>` for the package name and its exported symbols);
   check whether any such doc is in the diff.
   Violation (advisory): a package with a citing feature doc changed and the doc
   did not — flag it with the doc's path as evidence; the fix is updating the
   affected section, never appending history.

7. **Does any file break the bundle contract?**
   Detection: every content `.md` under `<docroot>` starts with a terminated
   frontmatter block (first line `---`, a closing `---` follows) carrying
   `type` valued `feature` / `architecture` / `guide` and a non-empty
   `description`. Index files carry NO frontmatter — except the root index,
   whose block is exactly one `okf_version: "0.2"` (required there, forbidden
   everywhere else). `grep -rn '^related:'` over doc-root
   frontmatter; `find <docroot> -name 'log.md'`. For every index line shaped
   `- [doc](path) — text`, compare the text against the target's `description`
   when it has one (⚠️-flagged lines exempt — recorded findings, not copies;
   bare sub-index targets have no `description` and are skipped); the script's
   `--fix` flag rewrites drifted lines from the descriptions.
   Violation: a missing or unterminated frontmatter block on a content doc; a
   missing or invalid required key (a `type` outside the three classes, an
   empty `description`); frontmatter on a sub-index; any key besides
   `okf_version` on the root index; a missing, duplicated, or mis-valued root
   `okf_version`; a `related:` key anywhere; a `log.md` anywhere in the doc
   root; an index line that drifted from the `description` it copies.
   Advisory branch: a doc whose `stale_after` is in the past (or
   `status: deprecated`) with no ⚠️ on its index line — recorded staleness the
   map does not show; the fix is re-copying the line (drift-check rule above).

200	## Godoc Menus
201	
202	**These are MENUS, not forms** (normative: R9's tiered comment-budget policy —
203	**1–5 prose lines** scaled to the symbol's role; blank `//` lines, the See-edge, and
204	short inline examples of 2–4 lines are free). The menus price **exported** API
205	only — unexported symbols default to no comment at all (R9's visibility
206	default; special case: one very-high-value line). The WHY is the default
207	content; the tier caps how much of a menu any one symbol can order:
208	
209	- **Helper** (small method, plain constructor, obvious accessor) → 0–1 line, or
210	  nothing; a tiny example only if it clarifies.
211	- **Contract** (parsing constructor like `ParsePort`, self-validating type, ordinary
212	  exported API) → 2–3 lines; a dos/don'ts example is free and often earns its place.
213	- **Crossroads** (entry point, orchestrator, state machine, feature front door) →
214	  up to 5 lines: WHY, architectural context, use cases.
215	
216	Overflow never stays inline — it moves to the feature doc; the
217	`See docs/<feature>.md` edge (kept whenever the doc exists) carries the pointer. A
218	crossroads that deserves more than 5 lines inline gets an expand recommendation in
219	the FEATURE report instead of extra lines — a human decides (R9's escape hatch).
220	
221	What fills the chosen menu lines comes from the [Comment Value Toolbox](#comment-value-toolbox)
222	above — every prose line must deliver one of its values, in plain English (R9's
223	three-test standard).

226	
227	Pick only the lines this package needs:

231	//
232	// [1-2 sentences: what problem this solves]              <- usually
233	//
234	// Main data flow:                                        <- only if non-obvious
235	//   Input -> Validation -> Processing -> Output
236	//

238	//   - Type1: [key responsibility]
239	//

241	//   - [Key decision and why]
242	//
243	// See docs/[feature].md for architecture and usage.      <- whenever the doc exists

570	## Bootstrap Classification
571	
572	Classify each inventoried doc; the class decides its index line, grouping, and
573	frontmatter `type` (stale is a lifecycle, not a type — it keeps the class it would
574	otherwise have, expressed via `status`/`stale_after` plus the flagged line):
575	
576	| Class | Signals | Index treatment | Frontmatter `type` |
577	|-------|---------|-----------------|--------------------|
578	| **feature** | describes one capability's behavior; cites its symbols | group under its topic | `feature` |
579	| **architecture** | cross-feature structure, system-wide patterns | its own "Architecture" group | `architecture` |
580	| **guide** | setup, how-to, onboarding, runbooks | "Guides" group | `guide` |
581	| **stale** | cites symbols/packages that no longer resolve; describes removed behavior | index with a FLAGGED line (below); the flag is the advisory finding | its underlying class |
582	
583	**Stale never means unindexed** — R9's Q1 reachability invariant always wins. A stale
584	doc gets a flagged index line naming the unresolved symbol:
585	
586	```markdown
587	- [auth.md](auth.md) — ⚠️ stale: cites unresolved `TokenVerifier`
588	```
589	
590	The flag names the unresolved symbol; it cannot tell an aspirational doc (written
591	ahead of the code) from a doc for deleted code — choosing refresh (FEATURE mode) /
592	remove / keep-as-roadmap is the user's call, made from the advisory report.
593	Bootstrap never decides.
594	
595	When unsure between feature and architecture: one capability → feature; the seams
596	between capabilities → architecture.
597	
598	### Frontmatter Migration (Brownfield)
599	
600	An existing network without frontmatter — wired by hand, or by a plugin version
601	before the OKF layer — is just another brownfield state. **Verify-or-add, never
602	duplicate**: a doc that already has conformant frontmatter is left alone; a doc
603	without gets the required keys, with `description` written as its index line
604	(add optional `generated` from the doc's last substantive git touch when
605	evident). An index
606	carrying frontmatter (written by hand, or by an older plugin version) gets it
607	stripped — the root keeps only `okf_version`. A `type` the
608	classification table cannot settle goes to the advisory report
609	(`type?: <doc> — class not inferable`) — never guessed silently. Same for
610	`conventions.md` and the check script: create or verify, and report a diverged
611	script rather than overwriting it.
612	
613	### Rung-2 Gap Criterion (BOOTSTRAP)
614	
615	FEATURE mode anchors R9 Q5 on the diff; bootstrap has no diff. Report a rung-2 gap
616	on exactly two greppable signals — nothing fuzzier:
617	
618	- **(a) Dangling intent**: a live code→docs edge points at a missing doc — the edge
619	  is evidence a doc was intended (surfaces from the Q2 code→docs grep).
620	- **(b) Undocumented front door**: a package with entry points has no doc citing any
621	  of its exported symbols.
622	
623	### Upward-Edge Anchor Heuristic (BOOTSTRAP step 5)
624	
625	Each indexed doc gets at most ONE upward edge (low density — R9 edge policy). The
626	anchor is the doc's front door, chosen in this order:
627	
628	1. **The doc's central exported symbol** — the type or constructor the doc most
629	   centrally describes: usually the first symbol its index line cites, or the type
630	   in the doc's title (`spanlogger-api.md` → the `SpanLogger` type).
631	2. **The package godoc** — when the doc spans a whole package rather than one
632	   symbol (`versioning.md` → `package version`'s doc comment).
633	3. **No confident anchor** → do not guess. Report the doc as `unwired` in the
634	   advisory findings; a wrong edge is worse than a missing one (it survives Q2 —
635	   it resolves — while pointing readers somewhere unhelpful).
636	
637	Mechanics: append the edge as the final line of the anchor's EXISTING doc comment —
638	`// See <docroot>/<file>.md for <three-to-six-word reason>.` Never restructure the
639	comment around it; never create a doc comment solely to host an edge (a naked symbol
640	is a Q5 finding for FEATURE mode, not a wiring target); confirm the package still
641	vets after the edit.

717	## Guidelines
718	
719	### Bug Fix Documentation
720	
721	Bug fixes should NEVER add changelog-style entries. Instead, update existing docs to
722	reflect correct behavior.
723	
724	**Approach:**
725	1. Find the existing documentation for the affected behavior
726	2. Update it to describe the CORRECT behavior
727	3. If no docs exist, write behavior docs as if the bug never happened
728	
729	**Example — Email Validation Bug:**
730	```
731	❌ DON'T ADD:
732	## Bug Fixes
733	- Fixed: Email validation now correctly rejects addresses without TLD
734	
735	✅ DO UPDATE existing "Validation" section:
736	## Validation
737	Email addresses must include a valid TLD (e.g., .com, .org).
738	Invalid formats return ErrInvalidEmail with descriptive message.
739	```
740	
741	**Example — Parser Edge Case:**
742	```
743	❌ DON'T ADD:
744	## v1.2.3 Changes
745	- Fixed edge case where empty input caused panic
746	
747	✅ DO UPDATE existing "Input Handling" section:
748	## Input Handling
749	Empty input returns ErrEmptyInput. All inputs are validated before parsing.
750	```
751	
752	**Why this matters:** someone reading docs in 5 years wants to know "How does
753	validation work?" — they don't care that it was broken once.
754	
755	### Managing Documentation Size
756	
757	Two distinct size rules — don't conflate them:
758	- **A single doc past ~500 lines** → split it into a folder (below).
759	- **`index.md` past ~300 lines** → map of maps (R9's index policy; form above).
760	
761	**Split signals:** doc exceeds ~500 lines; multiple distinct topics competing for
762	attention; hard to find specific information.
763	
764	**Folder structure for a large feature:**
765	```
766	docs/
767	├── index.md               # root map — links feature-name/index.md
768	└── feature-name/
769	    ├── index.md           # sub-index: one line per sub-doc
770	    ├── architecture.md    # detailed architecture, diagrams
771	    └── usage.md           # examples and patterns
772	```
773	
774	The sub-index follows the same one-line-per-doc form; the root index links it, so
775	every sub-doc stays two hops from CLAUDE.md (R9's reachability invariant).
776	
777	**When NOT to split:** the feature is cohesive and flows logically; splitting would
778	create orphaned fragments; sub-docs would be too thin to stand alone.

804	#### ❌ Over-Budget Godoc (depth at the wrong rung)
805	```go
806	// Scheduler coordinates periodic report generation across tenants.
807	// It was introduced after the v2 incident where per-tenant cron jobs
808	// drifted and overlapped, causing duplicate report emails.
809	// The scheduler holds a min-heap of next-run times and wakes on the
810	// earliest deadline. Each tick it drains all due tenants, submits
811	// them to the worker pool, and re-heaps with jittered next-run times.
812	// Jitter is +/-10% to avoid thundering herd on shared storage.
813	// Thread safety: all public methods lock the internal mutex; callbacks
814	// run outside the lock. Do not call Schedule from inside a callback.
815	// See docs/report-scheduling.md.
816	type Scheduler struct { /* ... */ }
817	```
818	*Why bad?*: nine prose lines — the heap mechanics and tick flow are implementation
819	narration (rung-2 material at best) drowning the two facts a reader at this symbol
820	actually needs. Reviewers scroll past comments like this, then miss the one that
821	matters.
822	
823	#### ✅ Trimmed to Tier (crossroads: ≤5 prose lines)
824	```go
825	// Scheduler coordinates periodic report generation across tenants.
826	// It exists because independent per-tenant cron jobs drifted and overlapped
827	// (duplicate report emails — the v2 incident); one coordinator with jittered
828	// next-run times replaced them.
829	// Do not call Schedule from inside a callback — callbacks run outside the lock.
830	// See docs/report-scheduling.md for the tick flow and jitter math.
831	type Scheduler struct { /* ... */ }
832	```
833	*The overflow moved, not died*: tick flow, heap mechanics, and jitter math now live
834	in `docs/report-scheduling.md`; the comment keeps the WHY, the one caller-facing
835	constraint, and the edge that points at the depth.
836	
837	---
838	
839	#### ❌ Implementation Details Without Context
840	```markdown
841	## Implementation
842	The CreateUser function calls validateEmail and then repo.Save.
843	It returns an error if validation fails.
844	```
845	*Why bad?*: describes WHAT code does without WHY.
846	
847	#### ✅ Context-Rich Explanation
848	```markdown
849	## Design Decision: Validation Before Persistence
850	CreateUser validates email format before database operations to:
851	1. Fail fast — avoid unnecessary database round-trips
852	2. Provide clear error messages — users get immediate feedback
853	3. Maintain data quality — only valid emails in database
854	
855	Email validation is separate from UserID validation because emails
856	may need external verification (MX record checks) in the future,
857	while UserIDs are purely format-based.
858	```
859	
860	---
861	
862	#### ❌ Feature List Without Purpose
863	```markdown
864	## Components
865	- UserID type
866	- Email type
867	- UserService
868	```
869	*Why bad?*: no explanation of relationships or rationale.
870	
871	#### ✅ Purpose-Driven Structure
872	```markdown
873	## Architecture
874	
875	### Type Safety Layer (Primitive Obsession Prevention)
876	- **UserID**: self-validating identifier (prevents empty/malformed IDs)
877	- **Email**: self-validating email (prevents invalid formats, RFC 5322)
878	
879	These types ensure validation happens once at construction, not repeatedly
880	throughout the codebase.
881	
882	### Business Logic Layer
883	- **UserService**: orchestrates user operations — depends on Repository for
884	  persistence and Notifier for communication; contains no infrastructure code.
885	
886	This vertical slice structure keeps all user logic contained in one package:
887	"group by feature and role, not technical layer."
888	```
889	
890	---
891	
892	#### ❌ Code Dump as "Example"
893	```markdown
894	## Usage
895	See the user package tests for usage examples.
896	```
897	*Why bad?*: forces the reader to hunt through test code.
898	
899	#### ✅ Inline Runnable Example
900	```go
901	// Create validated types
902	id, err := user.NewUserID("usr_12345")
903	if err != nil {
904	    panic(err) // invalid ID format
905	}
906	
907	email, err := user.NewEmail("alice@example.com")
908	if err != nil {
909	    panic(err) // invalid email format
910	}
911	
912	// Create and use the service
913	svc, _ := user.NewUserService(repo, notifier)
914	err = svc.CreateUser(ctx, user.User{ID: id, Email: email, Name: "Alice"})
915	```
916	
917	### Common Documentation Scenarios
918	
919	**New domain type** — document why it exists (what primitive obsession it prevents),
920	what it validates, how to construct it, where it's used.
921	
922	**New service/orchestrator** — document what business operations it provides, what
923	dependencies it requires (and why), integration points.
924	
925	**New integration point** — document what external system is integrated and why, how
926	data flows in/out, error handling and retry/fallback behavior.
927	
928	**Refactored architecture** — document what problem the refactor solved, what changed
929	architecturally, why this approach was chosen.
930	
931	### AI-Friendly Documentation Patterns
932	
933	**For feature extensions** — established patterns, natural extension points,
934	constraints to maintain:
935	```markdown
936	## Extension Points
937	- **New validation rules**: add to the NewUserID constructor
938	- **New storage backends**: implement the Repository interface
939	- **New notification channels**: implement the Notifier interface
940	```
941	
942	**For understanding data flow** — entry points, transformation steps, outcomes:
943	```markdown
944	## Data Flow
945	1. HTTP handler receives POST /users → CreateUserRequest
946	2. Request validation → NewUserID, NewEmail (self-validating types)
947	3. UserService.CreateUser → validates business rules
948	4. Repository.Save → persists to database
949	5. Notifier.SendWelcome → sends welcome email (async)
950	6. Returns: User struct or validation/business error
951	```
952	
953	**Design invariants** — document invariants that must be maintained:
954	```markdown
955	## Design Invariants
956	- UserID must always be non-empty after construction
957	- Email validation follows RFC 5322
958	- UserService assumes repository is never nil (validated in constructor)
959	```
